subject: Orbit Analytics — Urgent throughput reconciliation & SLA credit request
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@orbitanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Orbit Analytics Support <support@orbitanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Significant throughput drop starting 06/18 — immediate assistance requested

Hi Karthik,

We saw a severe drop in throughput on our production route served by Redwood starting around 02:45 UTC on 2026-06-18. Baseline was ~12k tokens/s; we saw sustained ~1.8k tokens/s with error rates climbing to ~6% (500-series). This impacted our ingestion pipeline for the east-coast region and caused downstream SLA misses for our customers.

Attached a small sample of the metrics export and request traces for the first two hours. Can you confirm whether this is a capacity/serving change on Redwood's side? We need:
- Immediate mitigation steps and ETA
- Preliminary assessment for SLA credit under section 4.3 of our contract
- Confirmation that logs and traces are being preserved for the postmortem

This is impacting a live campaign and we may need executive-level engagement if this cannot be resolved within the next 24 hours. Please escalate as needed.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Reliability
Orbit Analytics

[Attachment: throughput-logs-20260618.csv (CSV, 2.4MB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant throughput drop starting 06/18 — immediate assistance requested

Maya — thanks for the signal and the logs. We're taking this seriously.

Quick notes:
- I'm spinning up a dedicated incident taskforce now (looping in Laura and Marcus from Ops).
- Can you confirm the exact route name and any recent config changes on your side in the 12 hours prior to the spike?
- We'll preserve all service-side traces and export the scheduler logs; I expect a preliminary update within 2 hours.

Cc'ing Laura for operational lead and Marcus for kernel/throughput analysis. I'll also flag this for leadership if we need credits or remediation.

— Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Thu, 18 Jun 2026 at 09:12, Maya Patel <maya@orbitanalytics.com> wrote:

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@orbitanalytics.com>, Orbit Analytics Support <support@orbitanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant throughput drop starting 06/18 — immediate assistance requested

Karthik / Laura / Maya — quick ops update from the serving side.

What we see (summary):
- At 02:43 UTC there was a sustained routing shift: ~30% of traffic for Orbit's route fell back from the GPU-optimized pool to a CPU fallback variant due to a transient kernel mismatch during a scheduled kernel selector update.
- The fallback path had a smaller batch window and lower concurrency limits, which explains the throughput reduction and increased queueing leading to 500 errors when load exceeded the degraded path's limits.
- No config change on the customer side detected on Redwood's control plane; the scheduler did a kernel selection rollout that overlapped with Orbit's high QPS window.

Actions taken so far:
- Rolled back the kernel selector change at 03:10 UTC for Orbit routes.
- Temporarily expanded burst capacity for Orbit's Dedicated pool until 2026-06-19 12:00 UTC.
- Exported sampling traces to "throughput-logs-20260618.csv" (attached).

Next steps:
- Full postmortem and mitigation checklist scheduled for 2026-06-19. Marcus will provide a tech write-up with timeline and remediation steps.
- Recommend provisional credit discussion while we complete the postmortem.

I'll attach the telemetry snippet and scheduler traces in a follow-up if helpful.

— Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: scheduler-traces-snippet.txt (log, 512KB)]

From: Maya Patel <maya@orbitanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant throughput drop starting 06/18 — immediate assistance requested

Thanks for the quick remediation and the rollback. A couple of follow-ups:

- We appreciate the burst capacity until 6/19 but the campaign impact spans the entire 06/18 window. We will submit a formal SLA credit request under clause 4.3 and need a written estimate of the credit calculation methodology you intend to use.
- Please confirm preservation of all traces and any contributor timelines (who touched the kernel selector rollout, was it automated, and which deployment region rolled first).
- Given the business impact, our CTO is asking for an executive-level call to review remediations and timeline; would Redwood leadership be available Monday morning PST?

We will need the credit mechanics (percent credit per hour of degraded service and any caps) to reconcile with our billing team.

— Maya

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@orbitanalytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Orbit incident — provisional credit offer and exec call

Maya — I’m very sorry Orbit was impacted. I’m the head of Customer Success and I’m stepping in to help move this to resolution.

Summary of Redwood's position and proposal:
- Root cause: unintended kernel-selector rollout that overlapped with Orbit's high-QPS window. Full rollback was performed and burst capacity applied as Marcus described.
- Preservation: all traces, scheduler logs, and request samples related to the event are preserved in an internal incident folder and we will hand over exports to Orbit's SRE team.
- Provisional credit: Redwood is prepared to offer a provisional 20% credit on June 2026 invoiced usage for the affected route while we complete the postmortem. This is subject to final reconciliation after the postmortem.

Attachments: a short SLA summary and the provisional-credit-invoice draft.

Next steps we propose:
1) Exec call Monday 2026-06-22 10:00 AM PST (proposed) — Karthik will send the invite.
2) Postmortem delivery by 2026-06-24 with detailed timeline and remediation actions.
3) Final credit reconciliation completed by 2026-06-30.

If that timeline works for you we will treat the 20% as provisional credit immediately and reflect it in your next billing cycle pending the postmortem.

Again, sincerely sorry for the disruption — we want to make this right.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-sla-summary-20260621.pdf]
[Attachment: provisional-credit-invoice-20260622.pdf]

From: Maya Patel <maya@orbitanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orbit incident — provisional credit offer and exec call

Vanessa — thank you for the swift engagement and the provisional credit offer. We accept the interim 20% credit while we review the postmortem. A few asks before the exec call:

- Please provide the raw scheduler logs and the exact kernel-selector commit ID that rolled during the window. We will need those for our audit.
- Confirm that Redwood will not alter or purge any related telemetry until at least 2026-07-15.
- Request that the postmortem include specific mitigations to prevent rollout overlap with high-QPS customers (e.g., dynamic blackout windows, autoscaler grace thresholds).

We have added our CTO (Rajiv Singh) to the thread; he will join the Monday call. Looking forward to the postmortem on 6/24 and the final reconciliation on 6/30.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Reliability, Orbit Analytics

Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.s@orbitanalytics.com>
